provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1962 reads `Praesta,` where 1862 reads `■nRaesta,`; 1962 reads `omnipotens` where 1862 reads `omnipoX tens`; 1962 reads `natalicia colimus, intercessione` where 1862 reads `natalitia c61imus, intercessi6ne`; 1962 reads `nominis amore roboremur.` where 1862 reads `n6minis am6re robor6mur.`; 1962 has `nostrum.`; 1862 has nothing there; 1862 sets no comma after quaesumus and none after the opening ut; 1862 spells natalitia where the 1962 spells natalicia: orthography; 1862 prints the j-orthography (ejus); 1862 conclusion is `Per Dominum.`; the 1962 prints `Per Dominum nostrum.`; 1862 layer damage: the ornamental initial, and a column marker cutting `omnipotens` in two. Corroboration: 1922 Mame carries 11 November at PDF pp. 868-869; not transcribed.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Muneribus nostris, quaesumus, Domine, precibusque susceptis: et
caelestibus nos munda mysteriis, et clementer exaudi. Per Dominum.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.
